maria: heads-up — noticed a new pattern in telemetry: a sharp but short-lived surge of 429s concentrated on a handful of API keys over the last 10 minutes. alerts fired, but paging SRE every time seems noisy. can we propose a handoff rule?

aj: saw that too. looks like per-key token-bucket exhaustion from rapid retry loops in some clients. we need two paths: transient spikes -> CS queue + automated suggestion; sustained or system-wide spikes -> SRE page.

maria: exactly. current monitor is a single Datadog monitor that pages on >100 429s / 1m cluster-wide. it's triggering on these tiny targeted storms.

devon: +1. propose splitting: (A) per-key spike monitor: trigger when single key emits >20 429s in 2 minutes AND 429 rate > 50% of that key's requests. alert to #cs-ingest with runbook link. (B) system spike monitor: cluster 429 rate > 5% for 5 minutes -> page SRE.

kai: I can draft the Datadog queries. rough draft for per-key:```
avg(last_2m):sum:requests.status.429{*}.by{api_key} > 20 && avg(last_2m):sum:requests.status.429{api_key:*,region:*}.by{api_key}/sum:requests.total{api_key:*.last_2m}.by{api_key} > 0.5
```
it's a bit pseudo but we can translate to real query. also add ``exclude:maintenance:true`` tag.

ops-bot: auto-alert: deploy/infra/ratelimiter v2 rolled out at 1832104600 — monitoring enabled.

cs-lead: from CS side, noisy per-key alerts are bad. we'd prefer a ticket created with enriched context (top 5 endpoints, first/last 429 time, recent client IPs, quota window) and a suggested customer message template. we can own the first-touch for single-key issues.

maria: +1 on ticket + enrichment. also add a cooldown suppression so we don't duplicate tickets for the same key within 30m.

aj: let's also add a synthetic monitor that simulates a hot key ramp to validate the alert behavior before rolling change to prod. simple script hitting the API with a token until rate-limit kicks in. results reported to a test channel.

devon: for the dashboard: add a small panel showing "Top keys by 429s (1h)" + a sparkline of token bucket utilization estimated from `quota.tokens_remaining`. include a toggle to group by org vs key.

kai: putting a draft Datadog monitor JSON here for reviewer comments:```
{
  "name": "Per-key 429 spike (CS)",
  "query": "avg(last_2m):sum:requests.status.429{*}.by{api_key} > 20 && (sum:requests.status.429{*}.by{api_key} / sum:requests.total{*}.by{api_key}) > 0.5",
  "options": {"notify_no_data": false, "timeout_h": 0},
  "tags": ["team:platform","alert:per-key-429"],
  "message": "{{api_key}} sending high 429s — create CS ticket. runbook: https://redwood/ops/429-per-key"
}
```
please sanity-check syntax.

cs-lead: runbook looks good. add snippet for recommended customer response + suggested mitigation (reduce concurrency, upgrade plan, backoff guidance).

maria: action items: (1) kai to iterate monitor queries and add suppression + ticket creation automation (due EOD tomorrow). (2) devon to add dashboard panels and synthetic test (due Wed). (3) aj to update runbook with CS template + escalation matrix (due Tue). I'll own rollout and watch noise for 48h.

aj: tiny nit — for suppression use 30m dedupe for same api_key, but allow repeat if error volume increases 3x after suppression window.

devon: noted. also suggest adding a histogram metric `rate_limiter.refill_ms` so we can correlate token refill anomalies with 429 bursts. low effort to emit from the limiter.

kai: will add `rate_limiter.refill_ms` and a dashboard panel mapping refill latency to 429 rate.

maria: thanks team. after changes, we should run the synthetic test and observe for false positives. if stable, we push to prod monitors and update the oncall doc.

cs-lead: thanks — CS will prepare a one-pager for support agents so they can triage per-key tickets faster. ping me when monitors are in staging. :handshake:

ops-bot: monitor-change: datadog/monitors created in staging by kai at 1832105899. ID: 987654321

maria: closing the loop — I'll do a short postmortem draft if noise persists. otherwise we'll treat this as a tuning win. :+1:
